scope: Decide whether word-final -I is a productive or nonproductive HNK morpheme, a governed distributional tendency, or neither. Do not decide VANI semantics, broader semantic families, clause grammar or L03 curriculum in this gate.
upstream_decisions: B7: final -VAN is a governed narrow locative formative with NONPRODUCTIVE_CLOSED_EVIDENCE
B8: PARAZAMO/PARAZAMI has a family-specific closed O/I contrast only
positive_findings: All currently known-meaning audited I-final forms have action, verb-like, modal or intentional readings.
B8 provides one controlled family where final O/I correlates with a semantic contrast: PARAZAMO/PARAZAMI.
The correlation is strong enough to retain as an explicit analytical tendency for future evidence review.
limits: Only one minimal pair directly isolates final I against another final vowel within the same stem family.
The recovered registry does not yet define a universal part-of-speech system.
Several lexical glosses combine noun/action readings, so verbal morphology cannot be inferred from English/Portuguese translation categories alone.
Unknown-gloss VANI and VANUVALI cannot be back-defined from their final I.
A statistical correlation is not sufficient evidence for productive derivation.

options.description: Record final -I as a governed statistical lexical tendency associated with action/verb-like readings in the audited corpus, but do not recognize it as a morpheme and do not license derivation or semantic inference.
options.effect: Preserves the strong corpus signal while preventing overgeneralization; B8 remains the only governed internal O/I morphological contrast.

options.description: Recognize final -I as a narrow nonproductive action/verbal formative across the known set, without open derivation.
options.risk: Would promote morphology from a corpus where only one stem-controlled minimal pair exists and POS architecture is unresolved.

options.description: Treat every I-final form as lexically independent and retain no general analytical tendency outside B8.
options.risk: Discards a strong and consistent distributional correlation that is useful as audit evidence even if it is not morphology.
